A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LVFace study. All ten pages of each were inspected, with text and image extraction resolving rendering glitches sufficiently for comparison. Both contain three figures, five tables and Algorithm 1, and end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original LVFace evaluations on MFR-Ongoing, IJB-B and IJB-C, ablations in Tables 3–5, and feature visualizations in Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, ablations and feature visualizations reported for LVFace.

M1.justification: The three PCO stages, feature-expectation updates and cosine stage scheduler are unchanged. Equations 7–13 and Algorithm 1 specify the same procedure; removing pseudocode line numbers does not alter it.

E1.justification: Both use WebFace42M and Glint360K for training and the same MFR-Ongoing, IJB-B and IJB-C evaluations. Reconstruction, animation and anti-spoofing are newly mentioned as background, without corresponding experiments.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains UniFace, UniTSFace, TopoFR and Partial FC. Table 2 retains ArcFace, AdaFace, plain ViT and TransFace at the same backbone scales. The loss and stage ablation comparators also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The preprocessing, model configurations, AdamW settings, two 60-epoch phases with batch sizes 384 and 128, and TAR/FAR evaluation metrics are unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Both retain the model/data scaling, base-loss dependency and PCO-stage ablations in Tables 3–5. Figure 3 retains the same eight-identity feature visualization across initialization and training stages.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–5 and the Figure 3 images are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains LVFace's 98.49% MR-All score, and Table 2 retains LVFace-B's 97.00% IJB-C result at FAR 1e-5. Reported rankings and findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The problem definition, loss formulations, feature-expectation update and scheduler mathematics in Equations 1–13 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The claims about PCO/CSS, benchmark performance, scalability and VLM/LLM compatibility retain their scope. The introductory repetition of the challenge ranking is removed, but the first-place claim remains in the abstract and Section 5.3.1.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretation of scaling saturation, Mask-subset tradeoff and computational-efficiency discussion remain unchanged. The introductory change from 'underscore' to 'suggest' adds no substantive limitation or new interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a GitHub project address to the abstract, providing access information absent from v2. Implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 add ten background references covering face reconstruction, animation, anti-spoofing, cross-architecture distillation and center loss. This broadens context without substantially changing PCO's positioning relative to existing face-recognition optimization methods.

P1.justification: v3 expands the introductory opening, condenses related-work prose, removes a repeated ranking statement and adds an explicit Table 2 reference. The affiliation changes to 'ByteDance Inc.' The section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 loses line numbers, Figure 3 is slightly resized and repositioned, and text and references reflow. Printed page numbers disappear and an arXiv margin stamp appears. Figure/table membership, figure content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added project link provides an access pointer absent from v2, while the brief background expansion modestly improves contextual documentation. These are limited gains: the method, empirical evidence and scientific support remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish the linked repository's contents.
